You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

In your continual harness, entries created without global_=True belong to this session and are lost with it.

How to work, in every instance (follow this exactly): keep a library in the folder /home/USER/runs/paper/kimi-moonshot-arc2-hpl/stream/frozen/seen-p2/play/users/u099/system/state/workspace/programs, two files per task, named for its task id: /home/USER/runs/paper/kimi-moonshot-arc2-hpl/stream/frozen/seen-p2/play/users/u099/system/state/workspace/programs/<task id>.py, defining transform(grid), which takes an input grid as a list of lists of integers and returns the output grid; and /home/USER/runs/paper/kimi-moonshot-arc2-hpl/stream/frozen/seen-p2/play/users/u099/system/state/workspace/programs/<task id>.json, every demonstration pair received for the task, as a list of {"input": grid, "output": grid}. If the task has kept pairs, load them; if it has a program, run it on every kept pair, and if it reproduces them all, run it on the test input and submit the result before anything else.

# Collect all newly supplied demonstration pairs directly from the conversation log,
# validate the saved program against every pair, and persist the library and memory.
import re, json
log_lines=log.read_text().splitlines()
log_msgs=[json.loads(l) for l in log_lines]
received=[]
for rec in log_msgs:
    if rec.get('type')!='message' or rec['message'].get('role')!='user':
        continue
    content=rec['message'].get('content','')
    texts=[content] if isinstance(content,str) else [c.get('text','') for c in content if isinstance(c,dict)]
    for text in texts:
        if 'Demos received' not in text:
            continue
        im=re.search(r'Demo pair \d+ input \(\d+x\d+\):\n(.*?)\nDemo pair \d+ output',text,re.S)
        om=re.search(r'Demo pair \d+ output \(\d+x\d+\):\n(.*?)(?:\n\nSame instance|\Z)',text,re.S)
        if im and om:
            gi=[[int(x) for x in line.split()] for line in im.group(1).splitlines()]
            go=[[int(x) for x in line.split()] for line in om.group(1).splitlines()]
            received.append({'input':gi,'output':go})
known={json.dumps(p['input'],sort_keys=True) for p in pairs}
for p in received:
    key=json.dumps(p['input'],sort_keys=True)
    if key not in known:
        pairs.append(p); known.add(key)
(base/f'{tid}.json').write_text(json.dumps(pairs))
# The existing transform is retained: it reproduces every demonstration.
ns={}
exec((base/f'{tid}.py').read_text(),ns)
valid=all(ns['transform'](p['input'])==p['output'] for p in pairs)
print('new demos parsed:',len(received),'total kept:',len(pairs),'all reproduced:',valid)
print('memory methods:',[x for x in dir(rlm.harness) if 'memory' in x])
